2608.03701.title: LiLa-WAM: Lightweight Latent Reasoning World-Action Model for Robotic Manipulation
2608.03701.paper_summary: World-action modeling has emerged as a promising paradigm for robotic control, as it empowers models to go beyond reacting to observations and anticipate how a scene will evolve. However, existing WAMs often incur substantial computational overhead. Pixel-space methods often allocate substantial capacity to visual details that may not be directly relevant to control, while some latent-space methods require multi-stage training to construct the reasoning space. The resulting training cost can make such methods difficult to train under modest computational budgets. In this work, we propose LiLa-WAM, a lightweight world-action model that reasons about the future in a compact latent space and can be trained end-to-end on a single 24GB GPU. Its core design is a compact latent reasoning space jointly shaped by future-state prediction and action generation, which keeps the model lightweight while remaining well aligned with control. For task specification, we further propose the Visual Transition Token(VTT), a language-free task representation that encodes each task as a direction in visual feature space. Experiments on RoboTwin~2.0, LIBERO, and real-robot tasks demonstrate LiLa-WAM's effectiveness, achieving 90.48\% success across 50 RoboTwin tasks with single-GPU training.
2608.03701.paper_summary_zh: 世界行動模型已成為機器人控制的一個有前途的範式，因為它使模型能夠超越對觀察的反應，預測場景將如何演變。<lb/>然而，現有的 WAMs 通常會產生相當大的計算開銷。<lb/>像素空間方法往往將大量資源分配給可能與控制無直接關聯的視覺細節，而一些潛在空間方法則需要多階段訓練來構建推理空間。<lb/>因此，訓練成本會使這些方法在適度的計算預算下難以訓練。<lb/>在這項工作中，我們提出了 LiLa-WAM，一種輕量級的世界行動模型，能在緊湊的潛在空間中進行未來推理，並且可以在單個 24GB 的 GPU 上進行端到端訓練。<lb/>其核心設計是一個緊湊的潛在推理空間，由未來狀態預測和行動生成共同塑造，這使得模型保持輕量，同時與控制保持良好的對齊。<lb/>為了任務規範，我們進一步提出了視覺轉換標記（VTT），這是一種無語言的任務表示，將每個任務編碼為視覺特徵空間中的一個方向。<lb/>在 RoboTwin~2.0、LIBERO 和真實機器人任務上的實驗證明了 LiLa-WAM 的有效性，在 50 個 RoboTwin 任務中以單 GPU 訓練達到了 90.48\% 的成功率。
